title: Latency-floor fanout scheduler with per-key KV-warmup hinting
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Introduces a latency-floor fanout scheduler that reduces tail latency for heterogeneous request sizes while preventing KV-cache starvation via a per-key warmup hint. Motivation: Continuous-batching pressure and high fanout can starve low-frequency keys and inflate tail latency when large requests monopolize slots. This PR provides a scheduler that enforces a soft latency floor to bias small/latency-sensitive requests toward earlier dispatch, while still preserving throughput for batch-friendly workloads. Key design points: 1) Latency floor token: requests below a configurable expected latency are eligible for fast-path fanout up to a small window to keep tail latency bounded. 2) Per-key KV warmup hinting: request issuers may attach an optional kv_warm_hint tag; scheduler maintains a tiny in-memory last-access sketch and will preemptively reserve warmup slots for keys that have warmed-up recently or have an explicit hint. 3) Fanout capping by bucket: fanout is bounded per priority bucket to limit slot monopolization. 4) Graceful degradation: when capacity is constrained, scheduler decay ramps down fanout and shifts to prioritized leaky-window admission rather than abrupt drops. Behavioral changes: default latency_floor=15ms for text-gen short prompts, fanout_cap=8 per bucket, kv_warmup_reserve=2 slots per hot-key. Configuration is fully runtime-controllable via operator flags and Console feature toggle. Implementation notes: scheduler changes are implemented in runtime/scheduler/fanout_scheduler.cc with a compact policy engine. KV warmup hint tracking sits in runtime/cache/kv_warmup_tracker.{cc,h}. The admission path and continuous-batcher hooks were updated to consult the scheduler policy and KV tracker before building the dispatch bundle. There is instrumentation added to expose fanout_decisions, kv_warm_reserve_hits/misses, and latency_floor_evicts as Prometheus metrics. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag. Start in canary region for 48 hours with traffic shaping to 5% of traffic, observe fanout_decisions and kv_warm_reserve_hits, then 25% and global after SLA confirmation. Backout is a feature-flag toggle. Testing: unit tests for decision logic, integration test with simulated request mixes (kv-hot, kv-cold, large-burst), and an end-to-end perf job that validates P99 reduction on mixed workloads. Backwards compatibility: honors existing batcher contracts and will not change external API surface. See linked Linear tasks for evaluation prompt sets and perf dashboards.
commits: 3 commits: a) Add fanout scheduler core and policy engine (Sofia Martinez) b) Implement kv_warmup_tracker and integrate with admission path (Sofia Martinez) c) Add tests, metrics, and documentation (S. Martinez)
review_comments: Devon Liu: Concern about unbounded memory if every key attaches kv_warm_hint; asked for an LFU cap and eviction policy. Author: Added a fixed-size sketch with exponential decay and clarified limits in kv_warmup_tracker.h; updated tests. Devon: Requested additional unit test for eviction behavior; added. Priya Anand: Asked for clearer observability (how to tell if warmup is helping). Author: Exposed kv_warm_reserve_hits/misses and added Grafana example to docs. Marco Ruiz: Ran perf benchmark and reported 12% P99 improvement for mixed workloads but saw a small throughput drop for large-batch-only traces; requested fanout_cap tuning and a runtime flag to disable warmup reserve. Author: Added fanout_cap param and a runtime toggle; Marco approved. CI flakiness: initial CI lint failure due to style in fanout_scheduler.h fixed in follow-up commit. Final review: approvals from Devon and Priya; Marco merged with squash.
ci_summary: Initial pipeline: lint failed (style) on first push; subsequent push fixed lint. Unit tests green except a flaky admission_test which was re-recorded and stabilized. Integration perf job (internal) passed validation thresholds for P99 and CPU footprint in canary config. All checks passing on merge.
release_notes: Improves P99 latency for mixed workloads by introducing a latency-floor fanout scheduler and optional per-key KV warmup hinting. Config flags: runtime.sched.latency_floor_ms, runtime.sched.fanout_cap, runtime.sched.kv_warmup_reserve, feature.flag.fanout_latency_floor. Rollout behind feature flag. Monitoring: telemetry.fanout_decisions, telemetry.kv_warm_reserve_hits, telemetry.kv_warm_reserve_misses.
